events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Your favorite local public radio show Live Wire is throwing an afterparty for this year's Portland Book Festival on Saturday, November 7th at the Alberta Rose Theatre featuring a stellar lineup! Host Luke Burbank will be joined by veteran drag king comedian Murray Hill, writer and filmmaker Priyanka Mattoo, author and illustrator of Bojack Horseman Lisa Hanawalt, and award-winning synth pop artist San Gabriel. Show starts at 7:30pm. Doors open at 6:30pm. Live Wire Members receive 15% off. To get tickets, visit www.livewireradio.org/live-shows/2026117! ABOUT THE GUESTS Murray Hill is a one-man entertainment machine: comedian, host, actor, writer, and producer with decades of classic showbiz charm. Television audiences know him as Fred Rococo on HBO's Somebody Somewhere as well as from appearances in Life & Beth, Drag Me To Dinner, Elsbeth, Welcome to Flatch, and King of Drag. On film, he starred in Paul Feig's Jackpot! with John Cena and Awkwafina, and will next appear alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Man With The Bag. He's also reported for ABC News and Hulu's Pride Across America, and NBC News named him one of the "30 Most Iconic and Influential Drag Performers in Modern History." Library Journal calls his memoir, Showbiz! My Life as a Middle-Aged Man, “laugh-out-loud ridiculous, sweet and wholesome, and heartbreakingly poignant." Priyanka Mattoo is the author of the memoir Bird Milk & Mosquito Bones, a filmmaker, former Hollywood talent agent (UTA, WME), and cofounder of the women-led podcast network Earios. She's a contributor to The New York Times and The New Yorker and a MacDowell Fellowship recipient. Her latest book is How To Be Less Useful: The Joy of Inefficiency—a mix of self-help and memoir on reclaiming pleasure in mid-life and investigating why pleasure gets back-burnered in American culture. Born in Kashmir and raised in England and Saudi Arabia, she now lives in LA. Lisa Hanawalt is an artist and writer living in Los Angeles, CA. She is the creator of the animated series Tuca & Bertie and the production designer/producer on BoJack Horseman and Long Story Short. Lisa has published four books with Drawn & Quarterly: My Dirty Dumb Eyes, Hot Dog Taste Test, Coyote Doggirl, and I Want You. Her fifth book, I Can't Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex, comes out this October. Before he was San Gabriel, writer and music producer James Bookert contributed heavily to the recording, production, and arranging of the Whiskey Shivers’ songs that appeared on the soundtrack to the movie Pitch Perfect 3—collaborating with artists like Harve Mason Jr, Anna Kendrick, EsterDean, and Trinidad James. Following the release of the film, his then-band the Whiskey Shivers’ tour was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It is during this time that his new journey as a solo artist began, writing and recording his debut record Nights and Weekends while working at a liquor store in East Austin. This quickly caught the attention of Austin’s NPR affiliate station, who named San Gabriel “KUTX’s Artist of the Month” in January of 2022. A collection of singles later, Bookert started regularly touring with the band Goth Babe as a keyboardist, singer, and guitarist. In 2024, he was selected as the winner of Hyundai’s “Your Journey, Your Track” contest, and his song “Over My Shoulder” was named “Best Synth Pop Song” of the year by the PNW Music Awards.
events.title: Live Wire with Murray Hill, Priyanka Mattoo, Lisa Hanawalt, and San Gabriel

LILA FORDE With a voice steeped in jazz, soul, folk, and old-school American songcraft, the Seattle-born, Los Angeles-based singer/songwriter has always carried a deep sense of self through her music. But on Life Can Still Be Sweet, her sophomore album, that self comes into fuller focus: A little older, a little wiser, more instinctive, and more firmly in command of the world she's building. Warm, whimsical, and full of growing pains, the record captures Forde in the thick of her twenties -- chasing songs, learning lessons, finding her people, and holding onto beauty even when life gets hard. , "rdquo" -> I think I have a really unique voice -- not just my literal voice, but my proverbial voice," Forde says. , "rdquo" -> In this day and age, and in this industry, there's a lot of trend following, and there's a lot of homogeny. I'm just really trying to be my own artist." That individuality has been there from the beginning. Raised in a spiritual, music-filled household in Seattle, Forde grew up without a television and with her feet in the dirt -- the daughter of a musician and meditation teachers who encouraged her to stay curious, grounded, and creatively free. She sang in choirs, studied jazz in college, and steeped herself in the classics, from Bonnie Raitt and Carole King to Ella Fitzgerald and Nancy Wilson, while developing her soulful California sound that feels unmistakably her own. https://lilaforde.com/ --- Zan Fiskum Zan Fiskum is a singer and songwriter from Maple Valley, WA, whose music blends folk, soul, and cinematic pop into emotionally vivid storytelling. events.summary: Gram Jam is a celebration of the music of Gram Parsons. A seminal figure at the roots of what is now referred to as Americana. A mix of traditional country, rock n roll, blues and soul. Gram called that mix Cosmic American Music. Gram Parson's efforts with The International Submarine Band, The Byrds, The Flying Burrito Brothers and his two solo albums, GP and Grievous Angel were not commercial successes but his songs and style influenced all that came after. The Eagles, Little Feat, Workingman's Dead by the Grateful Dead, The New Riders of The Purple Sage, Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris are just a short list. Cosmic American Music is still alive and well in Portland and many other places around the world. Shorty and The Mustangs have organized five Gram Jam benefit concerts for the Jeremy Wilson Foundation https://www.thejwf.or since 2016. So why do a sixth now? In November, Gram Parsons would be turning 80 within two days of Gram Jam VI and will also be inducted into The Rock n Roll Hall of Fame within a few weeks of the show. In addition, Shorty and The Mustangs are celebrating their 30 th Anniversary in 2026. Too many dates have aligned. It's meant to happen. A stellar list of local musicians are donating their time and talent to this benefit show. Get your tickets, you don't want to miss this!
events.title: Gram Jam VI: A Tribute to Gram Parsons to Benefit the Jeremy Wilson Foundation

events.summary: Ding ding ding… your room is waiting at the infamous Hitchcock Hotel. Although decades have passed since the Hitchcock family entertained royalty and influential politicians, the hotel's dubious operations continue. events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: ROCKY MOUNTAIN HIGH EXPERIENCE® starring Rick Schuler Experience the music of John Denver through the artistry of Rick Schuler, the nation's premier tribute to the legendary singer-songwriter. Rick's story began at 13, when a pair of round glasses revealed a striking resemblance to Denver—and sparked a lifelong passion. That shy kid who taught himself guitar has spent nearly four decades bringing Denver's timeless songs to stages across the country, becoming the most celebrated interpreter of the beloved icon's catalog. A ROCKY MOUNTAIN HIGH EXPERIENCE® offers more than nostalgia—it's an authentic celebration of the music that defined a generation. Rick's heartfelt performances transport audiences through Denver's greatest hits: the sun-soaked warmth of "Sunshine on My Shoulders," the foot-stomping joy of "Thank God I'm a Country Boy," the soaring beauty of "Rocky Mountain High," and beloved classics like "Take Me Home, Country Roads," "Annie's Song," "Calypso," and "Leaving on a Jet Plane." Each year, thousands of fans discover why Rick Schuler's tribute resonates so deeply—his genuine connection to the music, his remarkable vocal and visual resemblance, and his dedication to honoring an artist whose songs offered hope, healing, and harmony to millions. Join us for an unforgettable evening celebrating the life, legacy, and enduring spirit of John Denver.

A ROCKY MOUNTAIN HIGH EXPERIENCE® offers more than nostalgia—it's an authentic celebration of the music that defined a generation. Rick's heartfelt performances transport audiences through Denver's greatest hits: the sun-soaked warmth of "Sunshine on My Shoulders," the foot-stomping joy of "Thank God I'm a Country Boy," the soaring beauty of "Rocky Mountain High," and beloved classics like "Take Me Home, Country Roads," "Annie's Song," "Calypso," and "Leaving on a Jet Plane." Each year, thousands of fans discover why Rick Schuler's tribute resonates so deeply—his genuine connection to the music, his remarkable vocal and visual resemblance, and his dedication to honoring an artist whose songs offered hope, healing, and harmony to millions. events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Run Time: 170 min. TICKETS $15 Doors 6:30 p.m.; Film at 7 p.m.; author talk following screening. Select Showtime to Purchase Tickets Click here to learn more about accessibility at the Tomorrow Theater. THE EXPERIENCE James Spooner joins PAM CUT for a screening of his film Afro-Punk, followed by an author talk for his new book It Starts With Anger. Books will be available for sale on site. IT STARTS WITH ANGER is a coming-of-age graphic memoir exploring race, identity, and rebellion through James Spooner's teenage years in 1990s New York into his young adulthood in the early 2000s. Confronted with systemic racism, microaggressions, and Nazi extremism within punk spaces, Spooner traces how reactionary anger evolved into a creative force and a path to self-determination, along the way following the founding of the Afro-Punk movement, his eventual decision to leave the company, and an ongoing raw examination of the tensions between underground culture and mainstream success. While not a traditional graphic memoir, IT STARTS WITH ANGER combines black and white zine-inspired visual elements including photos, illustrations, and cartoon panels with traditional narrative in a unique package that recounts the story behind Afropunk. James Spooner has not talked publicly about his reasons for quitting Afropunk previously and the book is a damning indictment of its corporatization. But more importantly it also oﬀers a look at issues of Black identity, representation, and the lack thereof in a movement that had often prided itself on allyship, while being completely myopic to all the ways it fell short in that regard as a scene that was ironically both liberating and alienating for the Black people drawn to it. ON SCREEN: Afro-Punk 2003. Directed by James Spooner. Runtime: 1 hour 6 minutes. This film, which many may assume is a historical punk documentary, actually is an honest and needed treatment of race and identity. Punk and Hardcore music is simply the microcosm in which it is told. First time Director, James Spooner, in telling this story, has opened new dialogues on these crucial subject both intra and interracially. Many times funny, sometimes sobering, a wake up call to America. An examination of the duality of racial identity that DuBois called "double consciousness." What could have been "The Bad Brains Story" is a story about kids, alienated by two cultures and two communities. Many of these punk and hardcore kids have never questioned their role in the punk scene or the black community until their interviews, and it's obvious as they struggle on camera to reconcile a fragmented self. ON STAGE: James Spooner James Spooner is an award-winning graphic novelist, filmmaker, and tattoo artist. His debut graphic novel, The High Desert, was named a Best Book of 2022 by Publishers Weekly, The Washington Post, and the New York Public Library. The book went on to receive the American Library Association's Alex Award and the Cartoonist Studio Prize. Spooner is the co-editor of Black Punk Now, an anthology of Black punk writers and comic creators. The collection was named one of the top music books of 2023 by Pitchfork, among the top five music books by The Guardian, and received a starred review from Kirkus. His forthcoming hybrid prose-and-comics memoir, It Starts with Anger, will be published by Pantheon Books on August 4. Spooner directed the seminal documentary Afro-Punk, which premiered at national and international film festivals including the Toronto International Film Festival and the American Black Film Festival. He also co-founded the Afro Punk Festival, which has grown to attract worldwide audiences in the hundreds of thousands. A Kickstarter campaign to restore and preserve Afro-Punk is slated to launch in May. His work has been featured in outlets including NPR, The Los Angeles Times, Vice, The Village Voice, The New Yorker, MTV, NBC News, and Variety. He is a recipient of the ReNew Media Rockefeller Grant, has served as a guest curator for the Broad Museum in Los Angeles and the Punk Rock Museum in Las Vegas, and previously programmed for the Brooklyn Academy of Music. James continues to screen Afro-Punk and give talks on punk, comics, authorship, and Black identity. TOMORROW T

events.summary: Daniel Nwosu Jr., better known as the Canadian rapper, singer and songwriter, Dax, is currently riding a wave of success with his Country-infused and near Gold breakout single “Dear Alcohol”. Initially sparked by his millions of devoted followers on TikTok, the single burst on DSPs and very soon after garnered a remix with Grammy-nominated Country artist, Elle King. With over 100 million streams to date, the viral song has found space between both hip hop and country music genres, appearing on numerous Billboard charts, Billboard Digital Song Sales, Country Digital Song Sales, Hot Country Songs, Emerging Artists, and landed on a multitude of Spotify charts, including Viral 50 \(US \+ Global\) in addition to other countries. Dax says about the recently released remix video with Elle King “it was amazing to join forces with Elle King on this remix and tackle a problem millions are fighting in silence. The impact is touching lives and this visual adds depth to already powerful lyrics.” “As musicians it’s our job to talk about all sides of life and I commend Dax for addressing this issue,” shares King. “I was honored to join him on this song to help shine a light for so many who are struggling.” The deeply personal single continues to resonate with people who are experiencing their own issues with alcohol addiction. Dax connects with his audience using his own lane of topic-driven music that generates conversations – and “Dear Alcohol” is no exception. A self-made independent artist for several years, Dax has garnered over half a billion streams on his collective catalog and has amassed over 13 million followers across his social platforms. As a proud Canadian, Dax was thrilled when “Dear Alcohol” was the \#2 most added record at Canadian Country radio as well as being announced as a performer for the Canadian Country Music Awards, happening on Sept. 11. Dax shows no signs of slowing down as he preps to hit the road and meet the new fans that he’s made with “Dear Alcohol,” all while maintaining a social media presence that only few in music have been able to master.
events.title: Dax

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/TTMOE26 On Sale: Friday, May 29 at 10am PT ---------------------------------------- The Tallest Man On Earth has captivated audiences using “every inch of his long guitar cord to roam the stage: darting around, crouching, stretching, hip-twitching, perching briefly and jittering away…” \(The New York Times\). Critics often draw comparisons between The Tallest Man on Earth and Bob Dylan, citing similarities in both songwriting and vocal style. Matsson himself has acknowledged Dylan's influence, revealing that he started listening to him at the age of fifteen. Fascinated by Dylan's covers, he delved into their origins, which gradually introduced him to early American folk artists like Pete Seeger and Woody Guthrie. However, Matsson is quick to distance himself from being part of any specific tradition, stating, “I don’t want to be part of a tradition. I just want to do what feels natural to me. This is how I play, and this is how I write songs.” His 2023 album ‘Henry St.’ marks the first time Matsson recorded an album in a band setting. As described by Matsson, it’s the “most me album yet, because it covers so many of the different noises in my head. Having been away from it taught me that making music and performing is what I’m doing for the rest of my life, and I’m so grateful for it. It has given me new confidence and playfulness. This is what I do. It’s unconditional.”
events.title: The Tallest Man on Earth

events.summary: Bombargo with Dylan ChambersSould Out Presents:Bombargo with Dylan Chambers Doors: 7:00pmShow: 8:00pmAges 21+. Bombargo is a Canadian based international touring band that drops a vibrant splash of soul over their distinctive vintage-pop sound. Well known for bringing unrivaled energy to the stage with sing-along anthems, double-brother harmonies, and a powerful message that combined make for one of the most captivating live shows ever! Frontman Nathan Thoens passionate conviction and Jagger-like dance moves even impressed billionaire and music industry icon Sir Richard Branson, quoting I havent seen this type of energy since The Rolling Stones! and he would know, having personally signed The Rolling Stones to Virgin Records.The band began with lead singer Nathan Thoen and guitarist Spencer Chilliak after the two spontaneously met and drove 16 hours to attend Sasquatch Music Festival where they became inspired to start a band. The duo wrote their debut single Let It Grow during their very first writing session and as part of Bombargos debut EP Back on Main which would go on to be included in The Top 10 Best Saskatchewan Albums of 2015 by SaskMusic. This further inspired them to continue writing, touring, and release their first full-length album titled We Are Bombargo. The group has since evolved into a 5-piece touring band adding Nathans brother Anthony Thoen on guitar, additional brothers Matt and Sammy Folkersen on keys and bass respectively, and Niall Cubbon on drums.Bombargo went on to receive massive acclaim when pop star icon Taylor Swift added their 2018 single Mr. No Good to her Spotify Playlist titled Songs Taylor Loves alongside mega artists including Ed Sheeran, Camilla Cabello, and Kendrick Lamar. Being the only unsigned band on this star-studded playlist saw Bombargo featured on CBCs the Q, NME, Exclaim, Fashion, Noisey, People, and Billboard. This success was followed up by the release of their most successful single to date Oxygen which pushed Bombargo into the Canadian Hot AC Top 40 Charts for the first time in the fall of 2019. The band also made its US touring debut in late 2019 with their 33 date North American Dream Tour which kicked off with Bombargo playing the sold-out Roughriders Labour Day Classic Half-Time Show to over 33,000 people. The bands highly anticipated US debut at Hotel Cafe in Hollywood, CA gained heavy press coverage including a raving article in Billboard Magazine.---Bombargo VIP, In Spite Of Everything Experience:- Early Access to Venue- Acoustic performance and hang with the band.- Limited edition signed poster and VIP Laminate.- Photo with Bombargo- Early Access to MerchVIP UPGRADE INCLUDES A TICKET TO THE SHOW.--- Notes on Seating: Open seating, may be limited or standing room only. Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21+. https://www.ericjohnkaiser.com/ ------- Known as The French Troubadour, Parisian-born Eric John Kaiser is a singer-songwriter reimagining French music through an Americana lens. Eric was born in the southern outskirts of Paris, in small town called Verrières-le Buisson, and began learning guitar when he was 10 years old. After years of a classical music education, he found a teacher that opened him up to the music of the Beatles and Rolling Stones. He began writing songs in his adolescence, using music as both a diary to channel his experiences and as his personal legacy. After performing over 350 concerts in France, Eric John Kaiser fell in love with a girl, a romance which would bring him to Portland, Oregon where he is currently based. Now, over a decade since his relocation, he logs close to 10,000 miles each year via air, land, and sea, guided by his music, exploring North America on multiple lengthy tours. He has gigged his way up through Canada and down through the South, as far as New Orleans and Boston. Eric John Kaiser has released six full length albums recorded in Paris, Oregon and Québec. His album , "rdquo" -> Made In Gaspésie" charted 14th in the , "rdquo" -> Billboard World Chart" the week of its release. He has performed at the de Young Museum in San Francisco, as an , "rdquo" -> Artist in Residence" at the Smithsonian Institute in Washington DC, the Blue Nile in New Orleans, and the Solidays festival in Paris. He has shared the stage with Welsh superstars Stereophonics, toured with French star Tété (who has also appeared as a featuring artist on his album French Troubadour), played with The Lost Bayou Ramblers in Lafayette Louisiana, as well as the French band Revolver. French Rapper Fefe from the band Saïan Supa Crew also appeared on Eric John Kaiser's album L'ODyssée. ------ JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.summary: SICK: A Year in Our Bodies Our bodies may be sick. Our lives are not over. Our stories deserve to be seen. SICK: A Year in Our Bodies is a fundraising showcase centering Portland-area sex workers living with chronic illness and disability---and the ways we have learned to survive in a world that wasn't built in our favor. For many disabled and chronically ill people, traditional employment demands something our bodies cannot always promise: the same energy every day, rigid schedules, eight-hour shifts, limited rest, and the ability to simply push through. Sex work can offer something different---the ability to build work around our bodies instead of constantly punishing our bodies to fit the expectations of work. We are dancers. Performers. Artists. Providers. Mothers. Hustlers. Creators. Disabled people. Chronically ill people. Survivors. This night brings our community together for performances, vendors, entertainment, and unapologetic visibility while raising funds for Rose and Pistolita to create SICK: A Year in Our Bodies---a calendar featuring 12 iconic Portland-area sex workers living with chronic conditions. Each month will put a real body and a real story behind invisible illness. Not as tragedy. Not as inspiration porn. Not as bodies to pity. As bodies that adapted. Bodies that worked. Bodies that survived. Bodies that are still fucking here. This project is about what survival actually looks like when your body refuses to cooperate with the rules of an able-bodied world. It is about the ingenuity of people who found another way when conventional systems failed them. And it is about refusing the shame that so often surrounds both disability and sex work. We are taking the bodies society tells us to hide---and putting them on the fucking calendar. Twelve workers. Twelve bodies. Twelve stories of adaptation, resistance, sexuality, illness, labor and survival. Come celebrate the people who learned how to make a living on their own terms. Come support chronically ill and disabled sex workers telling their own stories. Sick people are strong people. Disabled bodies are worthy bodies. Sex workers are workers. And survival deserves to be seen. SICK: A Year in Our Bodies November 21 • 8 PM • Dante's • 21+

events.summary: INFINITYSoul'd Out & Jack London Presents: INFINITY featuring Rhys Phillips, Matthew Snyder, Ben Landsverk, Eric Phillips, Brian Foxworth and more. At the helm of INFINITY is band leader Rhys Phillips, who contributes keyboards, guitar, and vocals. Rhys brings a distinct international composing background to the project, having created music for major global platforms including Disney+, Hulu, Fox TV, and the Calm app. The ensemble is further bolstered by multi-instrumentalist and vocalist Ben Landsverk (guitar, keyboards, viola), widely recognized as the founder and leader of Portland's popular Low Bar Chorale. Landsverk's extensive career includes collaborations with prominent musical luminaries such as Father John Misty and Pink Martini. Providing the core rhythm and vibrant vocal foundation are two exceptionally accomplished performers. On drums and vocals is Brian Foxworth, an Oregon Music Hall of Fame inductee whose formidable skill has made him a sought-after collaborator for Northwest blues and soul royalty, including Curtis Salgado, Linda Hornbuckle, and Andy Stokes. Joining him on vocals and percussion is Matthew Snyder, who brings theatrical flair and world-class stage experience from major national productions, including his featured Broadway tour role as Mike Teavee in Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and his acclaimed portrayal of Ricky Potts in Ride the Cyclone. Completing the line-up is veteran bassist, guitarist, and vocalist Eric Phillips, a founding member of the multi-platinum rock band Ugly Kid Joe with more than four decades of top-tier industry session work to his credit. A notable thread of musical heritage runs through the group's leadership: both Eric Phillips (nephew) and Rhys Phillips (grand-nephew) carry forward the legacy of their iconic uncle, Stu Phillips, the legendary composer behind the immortal television themes for Knight Rider, Battlestar Galactica, and dozens of other classic Hollywood projects. Together, this remarkable convergence of stage, screen, and sessionvirtuosity gives INFINITY its signature, unforgettable sound. https://rmpmusic.wixsite.com/infinity ------------- JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.summary: Isaiah SharkeyIsaiah Sharkey stands at the confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition, carrying forward a lineage that links George Benson, Curtis Mayfield, Wes Montgomery, and Jimi Hendrix while forging a vocabulary entirely his own. A Grammy Award--winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation---celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Born and raised on Chicago's North Side in a deeply musical family, Sharkey was immersed from childhood in gospel, jazz, and classic R&B. His father, a working musician, recognized early his son's extraordinary ear and feel, guiding him through professional-level repertoire before most children his age would form basic chords. By the time he was 14, Sharkey was touring nationally; by his late teens, he had already become a first-call session player in Chicago's tight-knit recording community.

events.summary: June McDoom with Eliana GlassSoul'd Out Presents: June McDoom with Eliana Glass Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21+. https://www.instagram.com/junemcdoom/ https://www.instagram.com/ladyliana There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoomʼs debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition. She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for. ----------------- JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.summary: Genevieve Artadi featuring Louis Cole & Chiquita MagicSould Out Presents:Genevieve Artadi , featuring Louis Cole and Chiquita Magic. Doors: 7:00pmShow: 8:00pm Ages 21+.Step Into GVA!!!! - Genevieve Artadis New Anime-Inspired RecordTeleport into Genevieve Artadis supersonic universe with her newanime-inspired record, GVA!!!!!Channeled by the kinetic energy of her anime favorites from Naruto, Bleach, Initial D, Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood, Jojos Bizarre Adventures, Rurouni Kenshin and Attack on Titan Artadis fifth album is my dedication to anime.Speaking on the albums inspiration, Artadi describes, The inspiration I felt was like being turned inside out, like some dormant dreams could awaken in a really fun and creative way. It was great to feel driven like this instead of getting pulverized by the worlds increasing grayness. Of course this would come out in my music and in a twisted kind of way.The album continues her signature fusion of experimental jazz with indie punk, dream pop, alt-electronic, cinematic ballads, and lush harmonic writing, but it is Genevieves voice and arrangements that crystallizes her beautiful expression into a future-sonic world that is truly her own. GVA!!!! is brought to life with her collaborators: Louis Cole, Pedro Martins, Justin Brown, Daryl Johns, Sam Wilkes, Chiquita Magic, Chris Fishman, and Miku Nakamura (of C shu Nie). GVA!!!!! is an energetic, rocking, colorful record through which I hope to bring a sense of ignition to peoples souls who hear it, explains Artadi.Out on all platforms this October 30, follow the release with her anime-inspired retro music videos and live tour dates with Louis Cole and Chiquita Magic.

events.summary: The Three Ds - A Christmas Nog IISoul'd Out Presents - The Three Ds - A Christmas Nog II Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages: 21+ The Three Ds is fronted by Jessica Dover on Vocals, John Dover on Trumpet, and Mike Doolin on Guitars. Since 2016, they have performed and recorded together putting their own spin on the music of Jobim, 80's pop classics, jazz standards, and a variety of Holiday songs. Their playful sound and arrangements lend a fresh approach to familiar material, leaving their audiences with a tap in their foot and a smile on their face. The release of their third studio album, A Night Like This, plays to all of their strengths. From the many hats of Mike Doolin laying down multiple guitar and bass tracks to every song, to Jessica Dover's breezy approach to Jobim's melodies, to John Dover's buttery solo work on the flugel horn. The Three Ds deliver a heavy dose of Brazilian jazz along with a couple of American songbook surprises. Their prior releases include, A Little Christmas Nog, and A Little Christmas Nog II: Nog Harder. Their holiday performances take the arrangements from these recordings and deliver them with a nostalgic banter. Add in the sound of their full band and audiences are carried away with a smile on their face and holiday cheer in their hearts. https://drive.google.com/file/d/16OvkjjkMWav-qqXpvyAHNDrI7rTiGm_0/view JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.summary: Kimaya Diggs with Lexie, Les AilesSoul'd Out Presents: Kimaya Diggs with special guests Lexie, Les Ailes Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21+. https://www.kimayadiggs.com/ When Kimaya Diggs thinks of green, she thinks first of her backyard in summer. Her house sits against woods that open onto a farm, and in the warm months the whole place seems to layer itself: trees over trees, native plants, birds, insects, and the deep living texture of land that has been tended carefully. When she moved there, the landscape was crowded with invasive plants. For years, she has worked to bring it back into balance. That image became the beginning of Green, her new album out October 2nd: a record about growth that has been happening quietly for a long time, then arrives all at once. , "rdquo" -> To me, green captures the seasonal moment when the first leaves come out," Diggs says. , "rdquo" -> There's no other moment where the landscape transforms so rapidly. The transition from summer into fall is very slow, but the transition from winter into just that moment of all the leaves coming out is so extraordinary to me. And it feels like some of the personal growth that I've made, which feels like it's taken a long time to come and then, when it comes, it comes suddenly." For Diggs, a musician, songwriter, poet, producer, and world-builder from Western Massachusetts, Green marks a moment of arrival. Newly off supporting dates with Mavis Staples, Emily King, Trombone Shorty, and Tank & the Bangas, she enters this album with a clearer sense of her own authority: as a vocalist, as a storyteller, and, for the first time in such a complete way, as the lead producer directing the shape of the record. Don't miss Kimaya's debut at the Jack London Revue on January 18, 2027! -------------------------------- Notes on Seating: Open seating, may be limited or standing room only. First come, first seated. Open dance floor may obscure sightlines.

events.summary: José James Sings Sinatra The celebrated jazz vocalist explores the legacy of one of the greatest American voices of all time. For internationally renowned jazz singer José James, this project is fate. In 2016, James was called by Universal Pictures to perform Sinatra's version of "I've Got You Under My Skin" for the blockbuster film 50 Shades Darker. James---a devoted student of Sinatra---accepted the role and soon found himself in the hallowed halls of Capitol's Studio B, behind the very microphone Sinatra used to record his most celebrated catalog for Capitol Records. "It was a huge honor and a surprise," remembers James. "There was a moment where engineer Al Schmitt brought out the famous Neumann U47, including the wooden box it lives in. On that box, written in black Sharpie in all caps, was just one word---FRANK. Sinatra was letting everyone know that this was his house and anyone who dared to scale the heights of his mountaintop had better be prepared." James rose to the challenge, performing that song onscreen in the film and recording another Sinatra classic, "They Can't Take That Away From Me," for the official movie soundtrack. Following that release, James has been in high demand, performing at the Hollywood Bowl Jazz Festival for both a Frank Sinatra tribute with the Count Basie Orchestra as well as with the Christian McBride Big Band. He also performed with Laura Mvula alongside the Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth Symphony Orchestras, and has been a featured performer with the Jazz at Lincoln Center, Royal Concertgebouw, and Metropole Orchestras. In September 2026, James will release his 14th studio album The Best Is Yet to Come, a groundbreaking reexamination of one of America's greatest voices from the most exciting male jazz singer of the moment. For James, this project is a reclamation---both live and on record---of Sinatra's brilliance as a jazz singer, a rhythmic improviser from the schools of Billie Holiday and Tommy Dorsey. With big band arrangements by the legendary John Clayton, this is no mere nostalgia trip, but a deeper look into the craft and mastery of the Chairman of the Board.
events.title: JOSÉ JAMES SINGS SINATRA

events.summary: New Orleans-based singer-songwriter Hans Williams makes soulful, dreamy folk shaped by the people and places closest to him. His debut album, Songs for the Neighbors, was born in the backyard o1f his Bayou St. John home, where late-night jams and intimate shows regularly spill over fences and through open windows. Recorded largely live at the house with his longtime band and producer Phin Choukas (Noah Kahan), the record blends folk with touches of soul, funk, psychedelia, and country. At its heart, Songs for the Neighbors is about connection with friends, lovers, family, neighbors, and those no longer here. Warm, intimate, and deeply human, the album captures the feeling of people making music together and Williams belief that even the smallest act of reaching out can bring us closer. Now, Williams is excited to bring Songs for the Neighbors out of the backyard and onto the stage. To play these songs live, see familiar faces, meet new ones, and share the record with the people who have been listening along the way.
events.title: HANS WILLIAMS

events.summary: The LiminanasStar Theater Presents: The LiminanasDoors: 8:00pmShow: 9:00pmAges: 21+ ----- Hailing from a small town in the South of France, Lionel and Marie Limiana aka The Limianas reinvent the 1960s French yy heritage by fusing it with modern rock.Their unique style blends the rebellious spirit and aesthetic of the Gainsbourg and Bardot era with contemporary garage and psychedelic sounds.Singing in French anas have a unique ability to distill the cachet of a nostalgic, highly cinematic era while revisiting it through a modern lens.

events.summary: Watch as world class drivers take Hot Wheels vehicles through a series of stunt challenges, with each competition getting more difficult and even more epic. Witness iconic Hot Wheels cars, Street Bikes, and ATVs execute precision driving skills, backflips, ramp jumps, take on the iconic 45 feet tall 360 loop and more! Featuring interactive fan experiences, larger than life Hot Wheels displays, and special appearances by legendary Hot Wheels vehicles including GT Scorcher, Boneshaker, Rodger Dodger and more. Hot Wheels Stunt Show is the next level experience for fans of all ages. Whether you are a die hard collector or a young challenger dreaming of racing glory, this show is a must see, edge of your seat experience for audiences of all ages.
